The gap

The lorry left. The invoice didn't.

A load is lifted at a terminal. Somewhere between the gantry and the general ledger, that movement has to become a bill of lading, a certificate of analysis, a freight cost, a sales order in SAP, a line on a reconciliation and eventually an invoice at the right price under the right incoterm.

Most businesses in this sector do that with a core ERP, a scheduling system, a terminal automation system, three spreadsheets and somebody who knows where the bodies are buried. It works, until the person leaves or the volume doubles.

We close those gaps. Not by replacing the ERP — nobody wants that — but by building the connectors between what you already run, and the operational apps that sit in the spaces the ERP was never going to cover.

What we build

Four things, done properly, for a long time.

01

Connectors and interfaces

Moving records between systems that have no intention of cooperating: SAP sales orders and invoice types, carrier and partner interfaces, scheduled file exchange, and the unglamorous work of making a transform survive a format change at the other end. We have migrated BizTalk estates onto Logic Apps and lived with the result.

SAP interfacesAzure Logic Apps BizTalk migrationSFTP & file transfer REST / SOAP APIsDataflows
02

Operational apps on Power Platform

Where the ERP stops, this starts. Freight cost capture with rail and road rates against quotes. Tank and product configuration. Order forms that field staff will actually use. Reconciliation between two sides of the same movement. Built as canvas and model-driven apps with Power Automate behind them, so your own team can keep them alive.

Power AppsPower Automate DataverseSharePoint Freight costReconciliation
03

Reporting that survives an audit

Railcar and fleet utilisation. Procurement. Inventory and stock levels by tank. Hedging and net premium. Freight reconciliation. Power BI models built on the actual transaction data rather than a monthly extract, which is the difference between a report you argue about and one you act on.

Power BIPower Query Inventory & stockRail & fleet Hedging / net premium
04

Order to invoice, end to end

Contract pricing and price bands, price lists that change mid-month, incoterm-driven documentation, invoice point logic, blended product on a single order, tank transfers between depots. This is where the money actually leaks, and it is the part generalist integrators consistently underestimate.

Contract pricingPrice bands Invoice pointIncoterms Documentation
Domain fluency

You shouldn't have to explain your own business to your integrator.

We have spent years in this vocabulary. On a first call, none of the following needs defining — which is usually the point at which people relax.

  • BOLbill of lading, and what breaks when it's keyed twice
  • COAcertificate of analysis, per batch, per customer
  • Invoice pointwhere title and billing actually change hands
  • Incoterm EXWand the loading instruction it should trigger
  • Tank transferbetween depots, with product identity intact
  • Blended producton one order line, reconciled to two sources
  • Railcar trackingutilisation, procurement and demurrage exposure
  • Net premiumand why the hedging report has to be fast
  • Price bandcontract fixed price against a moving list
  • Freight costquoted, accrued and reconciled against carrier invoice
  • Stock levelby tank, by product, at a point in time
  • Sales order syncthe ones SAP quietly didn't take

How the work runs

Our longest engagement began as a scoping call about tanks and products. It is still running.

The pattern repeats. We are brought in to support an estate somebody else built. We stabilise it, then start closing the gaps around it — order and commercial data flows, reporting built on transactions rather than extracts, and eventually systems built from scratch where nothing suitable existed.

These are not projects. They are working relationships, and the longest of them has outlasted several of the systems it connects.

  • Phase one

    Support and stabilisation. Case work on an estate we did not build — orders, contracts, users, SAP exports and the file drops that keep failing at three in the morning.

  • Phase two

    Order to invoice. Freight quoting, invoice point logic, COA handling, tank and stock configuration, inventory reporting and export documentation.

  • Phase three

    Reporting. Power BI for rail and fleet utilisation, procurement, inventory and hedging — modelled on transaction data rather than a monthly extract.

  • Phase four

    Platform build. Where the ERP was never going to reach: a Power Platform system for freight cost, purchasing and reconciliation. Thousands of hours in, still being extended.

Also, and not incidentally

We are a Salesforce shop too.

It is where we started, and we still run Salesforce estates as a managed service — administration, Tier 2 support, Apex and Lightning development, CPQ and price books, Pardot, and GDPR consent work. It sits here rather than at the top of the page because our sharper edge is what happens between systems. But if Salesforce is your core, we have been holding the pager on it since 2018.
